tasks.title: The mental model: filters
tasks.predict: If `.` returns its input unchanged, what do you think `.a` returns?
tasks.elaborate: Why is a program that takes JSON in and emits JSON out easy to chain?

answers.predict: `.a` looks up the key `a` in the input and returns its value; `.` alone returns the whole input.
answers.elaborate: Every filter has the same shape (JSON in, JSON out), so one filter's output can be the next one's input. That is what the pipe `|` does.
answers.explain: A filter is a small program that takes one JSON value and produces zero or more JSON values. `.` passes the input through unchanged; `.a` picks a field out of it.

tasks.explain: In your own words, what is a jq filter, and what does it do to its input?

answers.explain: `.[]` emits each element as a separate output; `map(f)` applies `f` to every element and collects the results back into one array. Use `.[]` when you want a stream, `map` when you want an array.
